subject: Deployment mode follow-up: SSO / KMS / Logging retention requirements
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Elliot Barnes <elliot@fintechco.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Recap + follow-up: deployment mode needs (SSO / KMS / logging)

Hi Elliot —

Thanks for taking the call today. Quick recap and a few clarifying questions so we can size the right deployment option (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private/VPC). Notes from our call: 

- Primary product use: transaction enrichment and intent classification for customer support flows (~120 reqs/sec peak).
- Data sensitivity: PII in prompts, cannot persist raw prompts beyond processing; audit logs needed for regulatory review.
- Identity / access: you want SAML SSO + SCIM provisioning for service accounts and RBAC with IdP-managed groups.
- Key management: desire to hold encryption keys in customer-controlled HSM/KMS for model inputs/outputs at rest.
- Logging/retention: compliance asks for structured request/response audit logs retained for 7 years (encrypted at rest) and ability to export logs to your SIEM.

Based on that, my initial recommendation: Dedicated capacity could work for predictable throughput and a strong isolation boundary, but because you want customer-managed KMS/HSM and private networking for log export + long-term retention controls, Private (VPC or on-prem) is likely the better fit.

A few items we need to confirm to finalize the recommendation and draft the next steps: 
1) Can you confirm whether keys must never leave your HSM (i.e., we should never have access to raw key material)?
2) Is the 7-year retention a hard requirement from your compliance/legal team or is it negotiable to e.g., 3 years with justification?
3) Who at FintechCo owns procurement for on-prem or VPC deployments (we'll need networking contacts and a PKI/HSM admin)?

If Private is the path you want, we can loop in our security eng lead (Rishi) and solutions eng (Vivek) to scope the connectivity, KMS integration (HSM vs cloud-KMS), and logging/export mechanisms.

Next steps I propose:
- You confirm answers to Q1-Q3 above by Mon 11/23.
- We'll prepare a high-level architecture + preliminary pricing for Private vs Dedicated by Wed 11/25.

Attaching the security questionnaire export you mentioned (stub: fintechco-security-requirements.pdf) and a sample SSO config CSV.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai

Attachments: fintechco-security-requirements.pdf (PDF, 1.2MB) | fintechco-ssotokens.csv (CSV)

From: Elliot Barnes <elliot@fintechco.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Maya Singh <maya@fintechco.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap + follow-up: deployment mode needs (SSO / KMS / logging)

Thanks Marissa — great recap and exactly the areas we need to validate. Answers inline below: 

Q1: Yes — keys must remain in our HSM; we cannot export key material. We expect any integration to support key wrapping or a protocol where crypto ops happen inside our HSM.
Q2: 7 years is the requirement from compliance (regulatory audit expected). Not negotiable right now.
Q3: Procurement/infra contact is Maya Singh (cc'd). She'll coordinate networking and legal.

Extra context: We prefer private connectivity (VPC peering or Direct Connect) for traffic to/from the inference cluster. For logs, we need syslog/JSON export to our SIEM and the ability to archive to our S3 with server-side encryption using our keys.

We'll need a draft of the architecture that shows where keys live, how requests are proxied, and what control we maintain for logs. Happy to set a technical follow-up with your solutions team next week.

-Elliot

On attachments: I've uploaded a short internal security note (stub) that lists our KMS/HSM model and SIEM endpoints.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Elliot Barnes <elliot@fintechco.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap + follow-up: deployment mode needs (SSO / KMS / logging)

Thanks Elliot — that's super helpful and clarifies the hard constraints. Looping in Rishi (security lead) and Vivek (solutions) to scope technical options. Initial notes for the team: 

- HSM requirement rules out hosted API unless we implement an envelope-key flow tied to your HSM that still preserves our no-key-access guarantee. Practically, that approach has latency and operational tradeoffs; we should evaluate viability, but Private is the straightforward path.
- 7-year retention means we need to size storage and provide export/archival pipelines to FintechCo S3 with SSE-C or KMS-wrapped objects.
- Connectivity: VPC peering / Direct Connect preferred; we need your network CIDRs and a contact for firewall/ACL setup.

Proposed immediate next steps:
1) Rishi/Vivek + FintechCo infra (Maya) — technical scoping call (30-45m). Options to cover: Private VPC deployment vs Dedicated with customer-managed KMS proxy.
2) I'll prepare a short doc (architecture options + pros/cons + rough costs) and share by Wed 11/25.
3) If Private is selected, Procurement will need a draft SOW and timeline (we typically estimate 6-8 weeks for VPC on-boarding + HSM integration).

Can Maya propose a few times for the scoping call this week?

Thanks,
Marissa

Attachments referenced: fintechco-security-requirements.pdf

From: Maya Singh <maya@fintechco.com>

Hi team — thanks for the notes. I'm available for the technical scoping call: Thu 11/26 10:00-11:00 PT or Fri 11/27 08:00-09:00 PT. Either works for our infra and security folks.

To help prep: attaching the short security note and our HSM make/model. Also include a high-level list of required network artifacts we will need from Redwood (e.g., public IPs, BGP info if Direct Connect, and TLS cert expectations).

We'd also appreciate a ballpark price for Private onboarding vs Dedicated reserved capacity (monthly commitment) so procurement can evaluate.

Maya Singh
